title: KS-2166: four kyc routes act only for the signed-in subject, or a platform role on the two reads
body:
**TIER 1.** A security surface (who may read, list, start and erase a person's identity-verification record) and a data-destroying route. Gated by a tier-1 Opus QA gate before any merge (gate 338, round 1: GO WITH NOTES at `eb7315988de5`); the merge licence is Wednesday's GO naming the head SHA.

Refs KS-2166

Ticket: https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-2166/kyc-four-routes-never-compare-the-signed-in-caller-with-the-user-they

**Merge slot:** kyc `index.ts` slot. Built on develop `fa2d60ca8cee`, which already carries PR 2211 (KS 1931, the erasure cascade). The semantic overlap with 2211 was its ks1931 test cells calling the list and the erasure with no signed-in user; their principal repair is the second commit of this PR (see item 4).

Four kyc routes took the user they act on from the path or the request body and never compared it with the signed-in caller, so any signed-in caller could read, list, erase or start another person's identity verification. The published spec already declared 403 on all four; the code never returned one. **Behaviour change for callers: a signed-in caller who is not the subject (and is not a platform role on the two reads) now gets 403 where it got 200 or 201.** No in-repo service or frontend calls these routes (a `git grep` over `Blockchain/`, non-test files: hits only in the kyc service, its spec, `docs/openapi`, `SCOPES.md` and `WORKFLOWS.md`); callers outside this repository were not inventoried.

1. **The rule per route** (as ruled by Wednesday on Seat A 29th's plan, 2026-11-12):
   - `GET /api/kyc/:id`: the subject (the record's `userId`, after the lookup) or a platform role;
   - `GET /api/kyc/user/:userId`: the subject or a platform role;
   - `DELETE /api/kyc/user/:userId/data`: the subject only. No platform exception: the erasure is irreversible, and the GDPR erasure arrives on the `user.erased` bus (`userErasedSubscriber.ts`), not over this route;
   - `POST /api/kyc/initiate`: the subject named by the body's `userId` only. No platform exception: the consent the route records is the subject's own. The body field is kept, a mismatch is refused, and the contract is otherwise unchanged.
   - "A platform role" is the shared `isPlatformRole` (SYSTEM_ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN, ASCII fold, a non-string refused), the one list this service already uses for the review route; it is admitted on the two reads because the platform reviewer must read what the review route decides. Not `isPlatformOrOrgAdminRole`: the kyc tables carry `user_id` and no tenant or organisation column. ADMIN, ORG_ADMIN, ISSUER_ADMIN, connector, an array role, no role and no principal are refused on all four.
2. **The identity:** `req.user.userId`, the claim the auth service signs (`jwt.ts`), set by the shared `authenticate()` on `/api`; never `sub`, never an `x-user-*` header. A token without a string `userId` cannot be shown to be anyone and is refused. One helper, `callerMayActOn(req, subjectId, platformMayRead)`, beside `foldedUserId`: both ids non-empty strings, equal after an **ASCII-only** case fold (A to Z lowered). A UUID's hex is case-insensitive and `z.string().guid()` admits upper case, so a strict compare would refuse a real owner; `toLowerCase()` would widen what is admitted (U+212A KELVIN SIGN lowers to `k`). The database keys on the exact text, so the fold can only reach rows keyed by a spelling of the caller's own id.
3. **The refusal:** 403 `{ success: false, error: { code: 'FORBIDDEN', message: 'Forbidden' } }` on all four. On the list, the erasure and initiate it comes before any statement (initiate: after the body parse, so an invalid body is still 400, and before the consent check). On `GET /:id` it follows the lookup, so a missing record is still 404. **Existence-oracle trade-off:** a non-subject's 403 on `GET /:id` confirms that the id exists; accepted because the spec declares 403 there, the review route answers 403 after its lookup, and the id is a v4 UUID the service mints.
4. **Existing cells whose principal changed (no assertion line changed: a counted diff of lines beginning `expect(` over the six files reads 0; the same count over the new file reads 34, so the count can fire):**
   - `ks849-mock-timer-stale-write.test.ts` (S1, S2, S3): its helper initiated as `admin` for a random subject. It now initiates AS the subject it creates; every other call (document, selfie, complete, review) stays the admin principal, so S3's `reviewedBy` assertion is untouched.
   - `ks1868-kyc-save-consent-unreadable-throw`, `ks1868-kyc-save-verification-unreadable-throw`, `ks1868-kyc-save-image-attestation-unreadable-throw`, `ks1868-kyc-get-verifications-by-user-unreadable-throw` (3 cells each): their stand-in set no user; it now signs in as the subject the file uses.
   - `ks1931-erasure-cascade-stops-when-the-verification-read-fails.test.ts` (C1, C2, R1, R2; second commit): its stand-in set no user. Without the repair C1 and C2 go red under this change, and **R1 and R2 stay green for the wrong reason**: measured with 2211's fix taken out, they still passed (a 403 before the read satisfies "no DELETE and never 200"). With the repair and the fix taken out they go red again; with both, 4 of 4.
5. **Doc versus code:** `kyc.openapi.ts` declared 403 (`commonErrorResponses[403]`) on all four operations while the code never returned one. The spec is unchanged; the code now matches it. The spec's description of who may call these routes (and `docs/openapi`, `SCOPES.md`, `WORKFLOWS.md`) says nothing of the owner rule: a candidate filing, not this PR.
6. **Left as is:** the erasure route's missing try/catch (gate 334 finding 2211-2, now KS 2185). The refusal is a synchronous `return` before the route's first `await`, so it adds no unhandled path; no try/catch is added.
7. **Mutants:** 18 of 18 killed, 0 survivors (each a one-replacement tamper of `index.ts`, run against the new file, restored by sha256): the check removed per route (4); the compare inverted; the fold removed; the fold widened to `toLowerCase()`; each conjunct of the platform exception and of the owner compare dropped separately (4); the exception put on the erasure, on initiate, or widened to ORG_ADMIN; the erasure check moved after `dbDeleteUserData` (killed only by the zero-DELETE assertion: the status still read 403); the initiate row keyed by the caller instead of the body; the initiate check moved after the consent check; `GET /:id` refusing before its lookup. A planted failing cell turned the run red (rc 1) and was restored by blob hash.
8. **Docs:** one fragment per page (`Projects Documents/fragments/{flow,cheat}/KS-2166-kyc-routes-act-only-for-the-signed-in-subject.html`). `node Blockchain/Dev/scripts/docs-fragments.mjs check`: OK (rc 0); a planted typed section number refuses it (rc 1).

## Not in scope (pre-existing; named for the board, not changed here)

- **(a) A refresh token works as a bearer.** The shared `verifyJwtRs256` checks the signature, the algorithm and the expiry, never `type`, so kyc's `authenticate()` admits the 7-day refresh token as a bearer (measured by gate 338, finding G338-2214-2: 200 on the list, `GET /:id` and the erasure for its own subject). It does not get round this PR's owner rule (another user's refresh token gets 403), but it stretches any bearer's life from 1 h to 7 d, and a SYSTEM_ADMIN refresh token keeps the two platform reads for those 7 days. The fix belongs in the shared verifier, not here.
- **(b) Upper-case initiate ids.** Initiate stores the body `userId` verbatim and `user_id` is TEXT with exact-text reads and deletes, so rows initiated with an upper-case spelling are missing from the owner's lower-case list and are NOT erased by the owner's lower-case erasure or by the `user.erased` cascade (G338-2214-3; from reading, not measured on Postgres). This PR narrows it (only the subject can now create such rows) but does not change it.
- **(c) The same missing owner check on the sibling routes:** `POST /api/kyc/:id/document`, `/:id/selfie`, `/:id/complete`, `GET /api/kyc/:id/result`, and the `/api/kyc/microsoft/*` router (G338-2214-5; reading only). This ticket's scope is the four routes.

## Test Evidence

**Touched:** `services/kyc/src/index.ts` (+54 -0); one new test file (83 cells); six existing kyc test files (principal only); two docs fragments. 10 files, +507 -9 (three-dot against develop).

**Ran** (an Apple Silicon Mac, my own worktree, an in-memory stand-in for the database and a real HTTP listener on 127.0.0.1; no stack; Node v26.8.1, npm 11.19.0, vitest 4.1.12, express 4.22.3, tsc 5.9.3):
- Red-first: the new file with this PR's tests and develop's unchanged `index.ts`: 61 of 83 failed, every failing cell named RED and no RED-named cell passing; every other file 94 of 94.
- The new file with the change: 83 of 83.
- Whole kyc suite: develop `fa2d60ca8cee` 17 files, 94 passed (94); this head 18 files, 177 passed (177).
- `tsc --noEmit -p services/kyc/tsconfig.json` rc 0; tsc over the service source plus its test files (a scratch config) rc 0 (18 test files examined).
- Pre-push hook (runs `scripts/preflight/preflight.sh`): second push (the first, 08:26:24Z, was refused by legs 14 and 16 on my tree's missing auth and api-gateway installs; nothing reached origin; relaunched under Wednesday's ANSWER of 08:44:00Z): "shell suites: 127 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (of 127)"; "PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed." Skipped: leg 3 (Spec-auth conformance), leg 4 (Path resolvability), leg 8 (Served-spec consistency), which need the local stack up.

**NOT run:** a running stack; a real token through the gateway to kyc (the proxy hop); Postgres (the stand-in matches statements by text); the `user.erased` bus path; Node 24 (the LTS line); a container build; any consumer outside this repository (the extranet, an admin console, Kintsugi or demo clients); the four platform suites (Schemathesis, Akto, Playwright, k6); every other service's suite (not run: nothing outside `services/kyc` and the docs fragments changed). This is a form change, not a proven cure: the refusal is proven against the stand-in, not against a deployed service.

**Migrations / config:** none.
